    Example: 3 → 7 → SHIFT → 9 sets 37 kHz. Scroll a knob, drag vertically, or focus it and use arrow keys. Pull DUTY / OFFSET to enable adjustment.

    Front-panel practice and model limits

    WAVE cycles sine, square and triangle. Enter a frequency, then SHIFT → 8 / 9 / 0 for MHz / kHz / Hz. SHIFT → 4 / 5 chooses the frequency-knob digit. SHIFT → decimal switches V/F display. SHIFT → 3 toggles −40 dB. Enable OUTPUT before SHIFT → WAVE for TTL. Push DUTY to reset 50%; push OFFSET to remove its DC contribution. Power-up restores sine / 1 kHz and leaves output off in this trainer.

    Preset loading may start with output enabled. The extra readouts and load checkbox below the chassis are teaching aids, not hardware controls. MAIN is modeled as a clipped voltage source with 50 Ω series resistance; its display uses nominal peak-to-peak voltage into 50 Ω. TTL uses an ideal 0–5 V waveform (the manual specifies ≥3 Vpp); TTL loading, edge timing, noise, accuracy and warm-up are not modeled. Duty adjustment is limited to ≤1 MHz. TTL and MAIN are separate leads with a common grounded return; the trainer retains the MAIN waveform while TTL is enabled and mutes triangle MAIN above 1 MHz.

    4. Instructor / student notes

    What this simulator models

    • Breadboard connectivity and user-created jumper wiring.
    • Resistors, capacitors, a UA741 behavioral op-amp model, dual supply rails, and a function generator.
    • Two oscilloscope probes referenced to common instrument ground. CH1 and CH2 share the same instrument ground in the real scope, so mismatched grounds are flagged.
    • Time-domain RC behavior, op-amp saturation, finite open-loop gain, a 1 MHz dominant-pole bandwidth model, and a slew-rate limit.
    • Oscilloscope vertical/horizontal scale, coupling, position, trigger source/slope/level/mode, sample/average/peak acquire modes, channel-colored cursors, automatic measurements with gating and statistics, arithmetic math, run/stop, single, autoset, save/recall, and help.

    What is deliberately simplified

    • This is a training simulator, not a SPICE replacement and not a manufacturer firmware emulator.
    • Serial-bus decode, LAN/USB remote control, Go/NoGo hardware I/O, printer/PictBridge behavior, and calibration procedures are represented in the UI but not electrically emulated.
    • High-frequency probe loading, noise spectral density, temperature drift, input protection, and other non-ideal 741 parameters are outside the teaching model.
